observations.attempt: Attacked the ticket named in the dispatch instructions hardest: whether a path-scoped key (no repository-root-level allow rule) truly sees zero tickets, whether a path-scoped DENY behaves correctly, and whether an invisible prerequisite can leak status or block/unblock a visible ticket. Read permissions.ts's canReadResource/ruleMatches to confirm a ticket's resource.path is always '' (tickets are pathless), so a path-scoped allow rule (non-null pathPrefix) can never match ('' !== canonicalPrefix and '' does not start with canonicalPrefix + '/'), and the Cypher's allow arm requires rule.path_prefix IS NULL identically — both layers agree. Ran the full ticketReadiness.test.ts RBAC suite: repository-root grant sees its tickets / path-scoped grant sees none (same test, both arms); a matching (root-level) deny removes a ticket; zero allow rules short-circuits to [] with zero graph.run() calls; an out-of-scope prerequisite is returned with visible:false, status:null and never counted as satisfied. Ran ticketReadinessService.test.ts's AC-6 test confirming the SERVICE-LAYER result (what the MCP tool actually returns) never contains the invisible prerequisite's id even via JSON.stringify, and that such a ticket is excluded from 'ready' entirely (fail-closed: an invisible prerequisite always blocks, it can never silently unblock). Independently confirmed via grep-level reading of permissions.ts that a path-scoped DENY rule also requires rule.path_prefix IS NULL to match a pathless ticket resource, so it structurally cannot remove a ticket a root-level allow already granted -- symmetric with the allow arm, and the character-for-character-identical predicate block to the existing GET_ONBOARDING_STEPS_CYPHER (confirmed via direct diff of both query strings) shows this is the established, reviewed precedent for pathless nodes, not a new gap this ticket introduces.
